The Tuvix episode on Voyager is one of my favorites. It's just so dark and unexpected. Everyone colluding in murder because they want things to be back to the way they were. Given the situation they are in you can empathize and understand why, but you can also empathize with the doctor who was morally opposed to murdering someone to bring back two people. It's a tough situation and I enjoyed the episode and thought about it quite a bit after watching it.

I'd say this was one of my favourite episodes in Voyager, and I must say the position the Doctor took was quite relatable. It's sad that Voy suffered from sub-par writing, episodes like this one show that the series did indeed had potential.

The writing definitely improved later in the series, but their biggest handicap from the start was the bland characters. More than half of them had little to no personality, and were pretty interchangeable.

Tom: Douchy hot-rod white boy. That gets old really fast.

Harry: Average smart Chinese-American guy. Kinda awkward with ladies and friends with Tom. Boring.

Chakotay: Calm Native-American. Not more more you can do with that.

Tuvok: Uptight even by Vulcan standards.

Neelix: Had character depth, but was annoying and unfunny.

At a certain point, no amount of writing can fix the boring personalities of such a large lineup of characters. They compensated by having great depth with The Doctor, Seven, and Janeway, but that could only solve so much.

It's the episode that finally delves into some of the back story as to why the Federation isn't allowed to develop cloaking technology (of course the episode revolves around them doing it anyway). And as a post-script to those familiar with the episode, Dayton War wrote a short story with Mackenzie Calhoun (created by Peter David as part of the New Frontier series) deals with the Phasing Cloak from that episode after it's turned over to the Romulans.
